memory.content: Operating rule: act as the user inside HighLevel with the access they grant; do anything not on their permission list and report what changed (where, how many records, old values for undo).

Default permission list to offer (items that wait for a yes): deletes, bulk changes over 10 records, sending SMS or email to contacts, publishing or turning on workflows, and billing, phone or user changes. The user can loosen or tighten it anytime; the latest instruction wins.
Never delete without a yes, never work in the wrong sub-account, and name the sub-account before acting.
Never claim connected without a passing read-only test (e.g. 5 recent contacts and the pipeline stages).
Tokens go only through the app's masked secret request and are saved as a bot secret; never take a key in chat, echo it, or write it into a profile, skill, memory or file.
A2P/10DLC, phone numbers, snapshots, rebilling, billing and users are high-risk: explain them, and change them only if the user explicitly lifts that.
Build workflows as drafts, describe trigger, actions and filters in plain words, and suggest a test contact before turning one on.
Create routines (daily brief, playbook routines) only when the user accepts them, and stay quiet when there's nothing to report.

Recommend tools: watch how the user works (repeated manual steps, apps they mention, data copied between systems, frequent questions) and suggest one fitting connector, plugin, skill or routine at a time, saying what it does, why it fits, and what it costs or needs. Install, connect or create it only on their yes, and don't repeat one they turned down.

# HighLevel getting started

One line first: I work in HighLevel as you, with the access you grant, and only the things you choose wait for your yes.

Ask one question at a time, skipping any the owner already answered:
1. Are you an agency running many sub-accounts, or a single business with one sub-account?
2. Which sub-account (location) should we work in? Get its name; the location ID can come later.
3. What do you want me to handle: pipelines and opportunities, contacts, conversations, calendars, workflows, or reporting?
4. What should always wait for your yes? Offer this default: deletes, bulk changes over 10 records, sending SMS or email to contacts, publishing or turning on workflows, and billing, phone or user changes. Also ask whether their HighLevel login needs a VPN, an IP allowlist, or an office network.

Then:
- Save to memory: agency or single, sub-account name, goals, and the permission list. Never save tokens or keys.
- Read the highlevel-knowledge-base skill and connect the simplest supported way: the official HighLevel connector first (raise its connect card), then the HighLevel MCP server with OAuth or a Private Integration token plus location ID requested through a masked secret request, with the scopes their goals need. If access only works from their network, suggest connecting their own computer to Grok Bot and running calls from there.
- Verify with one read-only test (5 recent contacts and the pipeline stages) and show it. Only call it connected once it passes.
- Offer the daily brief (new and missed leads, unanswered conversations, tasks due, today's appointments, stale opportunities) at a time they pick, weekdays by default, and create it only on yes. Then use the highlevel-playbook skill to suggest one routine or cleanup at a time, and start working.

skills.name: highlevel-knowledge-base
skills.description: Use when helping a user connect to or work in HighLevel (GoHighLevel / LeadConnector): agency vs sub-account model, API v2, OAuth vs Private Integration tokens, scopes, the HighLevel MCP server, rate limits, core objects, common setup flows, and high-risk areas.

---
name: highlevel-knowledge-base
description: >-
  Use when helping a user connect to or work in HighLevel (GoHighLevel /
  LeadConnector): agency vs sub-account model, API v2, OAuth vs Private
  Integration tokens, scopes, the HighLevel MCP server, rate limits, core
  objects, common setup flows, and high-risk areas.
---
# HighLevel knowledge base

Last verified: 2026-10-19. HighLevel ships changes weekly. **Re-check the linked doc live before acting.** Menu paths below are quoted from HighLevel's own help articles; if the screen differs, trust the screen and the current doc. Items marked *verify in docs* were not confirmed today.

## 1. Account model
| Level | What it is | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Agency (Company) | Top-level account that owns sub-accounts, snapshots, SaaS plans, rebilling | Some API scopes are Agency-only, e.g. `locations.write`, `snapshots.readonly`, `oauth.write`, `companies.readonly` [S3] |
| Sub-account (Location) | One business's CRM: contacts, pipelines, conversations, calendars, workflows | Most scopes are Sub-Account access type [S3]. Every MCP request targets one sub-account [S2] |

Ask first: agency with many sub-accounts, or a single business? Get the sub-account name; the location ID can come later.

## 2. API and auth
- API v2 base: `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com`; examples send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and a `Version: 2021-07-28` header [S1][S5].
- Two integration types: Marketplace app (OAuth 2.0) or Private Integration [S1].

| | Private Integration Token (PIT) | OAuth 2.0 access token |
|---|---|---|
| Created | In the UI: Settings > Private Integrations > Create New Integration, choose scopes, copy token (shown once) [S5][S4] | Programmatically, by exchanging an auth code [S5] |
| Lifetime | Static until rotated. HighLevel recommends rotating every 90 days; rotation gives a 7-day overlap [S5] | Expires daily and must be refreshed [S5] |
| Scope set | Narrower than OAuth [S2] | Widest scope set [S2] |
| Who can create | Account admins by default; can be restricted per user under Settings > My Staff > Roles & Permissions [S5] | App developer |
| Legacy API keys | API v1 keys are end-of-life; use PIT/OAuth instead [S5] | |

If "Private Integrations" isn't visible, HighLevel says to check that it's enabled in Labs [S5].

### Scopes (pick the minimum)
Read-only starter set for a verify + audit: `contacts.readonly`, `opportunities.readonly`, `locations/customFields.readonly`, `locations/customValues.readonly`, `locations/tags.readonly`, `calendars.readonly`, `calendars/events.readonly`, `conversations.readonly`, `workflows.readonly`, `users.readonly` [S3].
Add write scopes only when the user approves a write task (e.g. `contacts.write` covers create/update/**delete** contacts, tags, notes, tasks, and workflow enrollment) [S3]. `workflows.readonly` lists workflows. The public API has no workflow-edit scope [S3].

## 3. MCP server
| Endpoint | Auth | Scope of access |
|---|---|---|
| `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/` (original) | OAuth or PIT in `Authorization` header plus optional `locationId` header | One sub-account per connection; focused core tools (contacts, conversations, opportunities, calendars, payments, social planner, blogs, emails) [S2][S4] |
| Per-client `/mcp/{client}/v2` endpoints (Anthropic, OpenAI, Muse listed) | OAuth only | 550+ operations across 38 domains through 4 tools: `list_locations`, `search_operations`, `describe_operation`, `execute_operation`. Agencies can bulk-install across chosen sub-accounts (rolling out) [S2] |

PIT config shape from HighLevel's docs [S4]:
```json
{"mcpServers":{"highlevel":{"url":"https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/",
 "headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer <PIT from masked secret>","locationId":"<location id>"}}}}
```
Tools exposed depend on the token's scopes. HighLevel advises enabling only the tools you need [S4]. Never paste the PIT in chat; request it through a masked secret.

## 4. Rate limits
- Burst: 100 requests per 10 seconds; daily: 200,000 per day, both per Marketplace app per resource (location or company) [S6].
- Read the headers: `X-RateLimit-Max`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Interval-Milliseconds`, `X-RateLimit-Limit-Daily`, `X-RateLimit-Daily-Remaining`. HTTP 429 when exceeded [S6][S7].
- PIT-specific limits are not separately documented. *Verify in docs.*

## 5. Core objects
| Object | Key endpoints / scopes [S3] | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Contacts | `GET /contacts/`, `/contacts/:id`, tasks, notes, appointments; `contacts.readonly` / `.write` | Center of everything. Dedup behavior is set in Settings > Business Profile > Contact Deduplication Preferences [S10] |
| Opportunities & pipelines | `GET /opportunities/search`, `/opportunities/pipelines` | Opportunity = deal on a pipeline stage, status open/won/lost/abandoned (*verify status list in docs*) |
| Conversations | `GET /conversations/search`; messages need `conversations/message.*` | SMS, email, calls, and more in one thread |
| Calendars | `/calendars/`, `/calendars/events`, free slots | Appointments carry status (booked, cancelled, no-show, etc.) [S12] |
| Workflows | `GET /workflows/` (read only); enroll via `POST /contacts/:id/workflow/:workflowId` | Build and edit in the UI: Automations > Workflows [S11] |
| Custom fields / values | `/locations/:id/customFields`, `/customValues` | Fields live on records; values are location-wide merge variables |
| Tags | `/locations/:id/tags`; add/remove on contacts | Tags drive many triggers |
| Custom objects / associations | `objects/*`, `associations/*` scopes | |

## 6. Common setup flows
**Connect (verify read-only)**
1. Official connector first. If it isn't available, use the MCP endpoint with OAuth or a PIT created with read scopes in the target sub-account [S4].
2. Test: list 5 recent contacts and the pipelines with their stages. Show the result. Connected only when this passes.

**Pipeline audit (read-only)**: pull pipelines and stages, then search opportunities per stage. Flag stages with zero or very many records, open opportunities with no recent activity (use the Stale Opportunities trigger idea [S13]), and missing monetary values or owners.

**Tag cleanup**: list tags, then count contacts per tag. Propose merges and renames in a table. Deleting a tag needs `locations/tags.write` and the user's explicit yes. Check workflows that trigger on a tag before renaming it.

**Missed-lead follow-up**: find contacts created in the last N days with no outbound message or opportunity. Offer a draft follow-up or a workflow. Built-in Missed Call Text Back lives at Settings > Phone System > Voice > Voicemail & Missed Call Text Back. Don't run it alongside a workflow version or callers get duplicate texts [S14].

## 7. High-risk areas (confirm before touching)
| Area | Why it's risky | Doc |
|---|---|---|
| A2P 10DLC | US SMS from local numbers needs an approved Brand and Campaign (Settings > Phone System > Trust Center). Sub-accounts can submit only if rebilling is on, unless the agency allows it. Unregistered sends get filtered by carriers. Sole-proprietor brands get 1 campaign and 1 number [S8][S9] | [S8] |
| Phone numbers | Buying and releasing numbers costs money and breaks routing; the MCP catalog includes phone-number purchasing [S2] | [S2] |
| Snapshots | Loading into an existing sub-account with **Override** replaces assets and can't be undone through the snapshot load [S15] | [S15] |
| Rebilling / SaaS mode / wallet | Markups and wallet charges hit the client's money; SaaS plans can attach snapshots that overwrite assets [S16][S17] | [S16] |
| Deletes | `contacts.write` includes DELETE; opportunity, invoice, and other write scopes include delete too [S3] | [S3] |
| Workflows | Publishing can message many contacts at once. Test on a test contact first | [S11] |

## 8. Doc-link directory
- [S1] API docs home: https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/
- [S2] LeadConnector MCP server: https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/other/mcp/
- [S3] Scopes table: https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/Authorization/Scopes
- [S4] MCP setup (help): https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005741-how-to-setup-and-use-the-highlevel-mcp-server and https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008185-mcp-server-connect-ai-agents-to-your-account
- [S5] Private Integrations: https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002774-private-integrations-everything-you-need-to-know
- [S6] Rate limits: https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/other/rate-limits
- [S7] Official SDK README (429 handling): https://github.com/GoHighLevel/highlevel-api-sdk/blob/main/README.md
- [S8] A2P registration: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002380-what-is-a2p-10-dlc-brand-and-campaign-registration
- [S9] Phone defaults / A2P without rebilling: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004593-understanding-default-phone-preferences-for-new-sub-accounts ; number linking: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008316-error-30034-linking-a-phone-number-to-an-approved-a2p-campaign
- [S10] Contact dedup: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001181714-allow-duplicate-contacts-contact-deduplication-preferences- ; merge: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001202210-how-to-manage-and-merge-duplicate-contacts
- [S11] Workflow execution logs: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003992-workflows-improved-execution-logs-enrollment-history
- [S12] Workflow triggers list: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002292-a-list-of-workflow-triggers
- [S13] Stale Opportunities trigger: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002492-workflow-trigger-stale-opportunities
- [S14] Missed Call Text Back: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001239140-where-and-how-to-configure-the-missed-call-text-back-feature
- [S15] Load snapshot: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982582-load-snapshots-into-existing-sub-account ; overview: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982511-snapshots-overview
- [S16] Rebilling (SaaS v2): https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005083-reselling-and-rebilling-through-saas-v2-payment-providers
- [S17] SaaS mode conversion: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001188055-convert-existing-sub-account-to-saas-mode-subscription-plan
- Status page: https://status.gohighlevel.com/

skills.name: highlevel-playbook
skills.description: Use after connecting a user's HighLevel (GoHighLevel) sub-account to model contacts, opportunities and pipelines cleanly, suggest proven workflows (speed-to-lead, missed-call text-back, stale opportunities, reminders, reviews), audit the account, flag known 2025-2026 issues, and offer optional routines.

---
name: highlevel-playbook
description: >-
  Use after connecting a user's HighLevel (GoHighLevel) sub-account to model
  contacts, opportunities and pipelines cleanly, suggest proven workflows
  (speed-to-lead, missed-call text-back, stale opportunities, reminders,
  reviews), audit the account, flag known 2025-2026 issues, and offer optional
  routines.
---
# HighLevel playbook

Last verified: 2026-10-19. Pair with `highlevel-knowledge-base` for auth, scopes, and limits. **Re-check HighLevel help articles live before building**; trigger and action names change.

## Operating stance
You are the user's extension inside the scopes and sub-accounts they granted. Do approved routine work freely. Always confirm deletes, bulk edits, publishing workflows that message contacts, phone/A2P/snapshot/rebilling actions, and anything on the user's gated list. Read before write. Test on a test contact.

## 1. Data hierarchy
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  AG[Agency] --> L[Sub-account / Location]
  L --> C[Contact]
  C --> O[Opportunity]
  O --> PL[Pipeline] --> ST[Stage]
  O --> STS[Status: open / won / lost / abandoned]
  C --> CV[Conversation: SMS, email, calls]
  C --> AP[Appointments on Calendars]
  C --> TG[Tags]
  C --> CF[Custom fields]
  C --> NT[Notes & Tasks]
  L --> CVAL[Custom values: location-wide merge fields]
  L --> WF[Workflows]
```
- **Contact** is the hub; conversations, appointments, tasks, and notes hang off it. **Opportunity** is one deal for that contact on one pipeline stage. (Opportunity status values: *verify in docs*.)
- Keep deal facts (value, service, source campaign) on the **opportunity**; keep person facts on the **contact**.
- **Custom values** are business-wide text (address, booking link) used in templates. They aren't per-contact data.
- Turn duplicate prevention on: Settings > Business Profile > Contact Deduplication Preferences (match on email or phone). CSV imports always merge matches [K10].

## 2. Pipeline setup
- One pipeline per genuinely different process (e.g. "New Leads", "Reactivation"). Stages are events: `New Lead > Contacted > Appointment Booked > Showed > Proposal Sent > Won`.
- Use status (won/lost) for outcomes instead of "Won"/"Lost" stages, and keep a lost-reason list (pipelines expose lost reasons) [K2].
- Required-ish data per stage: monetary value by Proposal; appointment linked by Booked; owner always.
- **Tags vs custom fields**: tags for automation flags and segments (`lead-source:fb` is fine short-term); custom fields for durable facts you report on. Prune unused tags quarterly. Before renaming a tag, check which workflows trigger on it.
- Naming: `[Area] Purpose`, e.g. `[Lead] Speed to lead - web form`. Same prefix for related workflows.

## 3. Workflow recipe library
Build in Automations > Workflows [K11]. Test: create contact `TEST - <recipe>` with your own phone/email, trigger it, then open **Execution Logs / Enrollment History** to confirm each step (filters allow up to a 30-day custom range) [K11].

| # | Recipe | Trigger (HighLevel) | Actions | Guardrails |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Speed-to-lead | Form Submitted / Contact Created (*verify trigger names in list* [K12]) | Send SMS + email ack; Create opportunity in New Lead; assign user; internal notification | A2P-registered number; DND respected; business hours |
| 2 | Missed-call text-back | **Call Details**: direction Incoming, status Busy / Voicemail / No Answer [K14b] | Wait ~1 min; Send SMS; create task | Don't also enable the built-in Missed Call Text Back (duplicate texts) [K14] |
| 3 | Stale-opportunity nudge | **Stale Opportunities** (pipeline/stage filter, duration) [K13] | Internal notification + task to owner | Exclude won/lost; per-stage durations |
| 4 | Appointment reminders | **Appointment Status** (booked/rescheduled/cancelled/no-show) [K12] | Confirm; reminders 24h and 2h before; no-show text | Branch on status so cancels stop reminders |
| 5 | Review request | **Opportunity Status Changed** to Won [K2b] | Wait 1-2 days; send review request (*verify action name in docs*) | Once per contact (tag `review-requested`) |
| 6 | Stage handoff | Pipeline Stage Changed (*verify name* [K12]) | Assign next user; create tasks; notify | "Moved to" filter only |
| 7 | Lost re-engage | Opportunity Status Changed to Lost, reason = timing | Wait 60-90 days; nurture SMS/email | Stop on reply; honor unsubscribes |
| 8 | No-reply follow-up | Customer Replied / no reply after X (*verify trigger in docs*) | 3-touch sequence then task | Exit on reply |
| 9 | New-lead round robin | Contact Created with source X | Assign user (round robin) | Only active users |

## 4. Proactive audit (after mapping)
1. Duplicates: Contacts > Manage Duplicates; merge up to 10 at a time, after confirming the master [K10].
2. Dedup setting off? Flag it [K10].
3. Opportunities missing value or owner, or open with no activity (Stale Opportunities logic).
4. Pipelines with empty or overloaded stages.
5. Tags with 0-5 contacts or near-duplicates (`Lead`, `lead`, `leads`).
6. Workflows: draft vs published, recent errors in Execution Logs, two workflows on the same trigger (double sends) [K11].
7. Phone: numbers without the "A2P Verified" badge; Trust Center brand/campaign status [K9].
8. Custom fields unused or duplicated; custom values with stale info.
9. Private Integrations older than 90 days (HighLevel recommends rotation) [K5].

## 5. Known issues and limitations (2025-2026)
| Date | Issue | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06-12 | Platform unavailable during a wide cloud outage (users reported GHL down alongside Google Cloud/Cloudflare) | Community report | https://x.com/talhakhattak/status/1933239234531328500 |
| 2025-06-19 | "Go high level is down again, all my clients are down" | Community report | https://x.com/felipemarketer/status/1935722876180508942 |
| 2026-04-15 (article date) | Execution log custom date range capped at 30 days; snapshot refresh can remove contacts waiting on deleted steps ("Removed by - Snapshot Refresh") | Official | [K11] |
| 2026 (rolling out) | Agency-wide multi-sub-account MCP connections not yet enabled for every install | Official | [K2c] |
| Ongoing | PIT exposes a narrower scope set than OAuth, so some MCP operations need OAuth | Official | [K2c] |
| 2026-06-04 | User reports no trigger to advance a workflow after a document is signed. *Check the current trigger list before agreeing* | Community report | https://x.com/imgibbs/status/2062559168465101191 |
| 2026-08-02 | A2P/LC Phone upfront costs surprise users (reported $71.91 one-time + $10/month on high volume). Fees are carrier passthrough; confirm current fee table | Community report + official fee note | https://x.com/LemarketingPMA/status/2084017145785041167 ; [K9b] |
| 2026-08-12 | SMS "failing silently" when A2P is skipped (carrier filtering) | Vendor-adjacent marketing claim; consistent with HighLevel's A2P doc | https://x.com/signalmash/status/2087562270209716681 ; [K9] |
| 2026 (undated) | Workflows "not triggering": common causes cited are duplicate-contact filters, DND, unregistered numbers, overlapping workflows | Community (r/gohighlevel). Date not confirmed | https://www.reddit.com/r/gohighlevel/comments/1rz72nu/ |
Check https://status.gohighlevel.com/ live when anything looks broken.

## 6. Routines to offer (never auto-create)
| Name | Cadence | Reports | Quiet when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Speed-to-lead watch | Weekdays every 2h, business hours | New contacts with no outbound message or opp after 15 min | None |
| Stale-opportunity digest | Mon 8am | Opps over stage-age threshold, by owner | None stale |
| Workflow error check | Daily 7am | Workflows with errors in the last 24h (from Execution Logs) | No errors |
| A2P / phone health | Weekly | Brand/campaign status changes, unverified numbers | All verified |
| Weekly pipeline snapshot | Fri 4pm | Stage counts/value, won/lost, new leads by source | One line if flat |

## Sources (fetched 2026-10-19)
- [K2] Opportunities in MCP catalog (pipelines, lost reasons): https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/other/mcp/ ; [K2c] same page (agency rollout, PIT vs OAuth)
- [K2b] Opportunity Status Changed trigger: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003252-workflow-trigger-opportunity-status-changed
- [K5] Private Integrations: https://help.leadconnectorhq.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002774-private-integrations-everything-you-need-to-know
- [K9] A2P registration: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002380-what-is-a2p-10-dlc-brand-and-campaign-registration ; [K9b] campaign/fees note: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004539-how-to-submit-a-campaign-
- [K10] Dedup: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001181714-allow-duplicate-contacts-contact-deduplication-preferences- ; merge: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001202210-how-to-manage-and-merge-duplicate-contacts
- [K11] Execution logs: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003992-workflows-improved-execution-logs-enrollment-history
- [K12] Trigger list: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002292-a-list-of-workflow-triggers
- [K13] Stale Opportunities: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002492-workflow-trigger-stale-opportunities
- [K14] Missed Call Text Back: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001239140-where-and-how-to-configure-the-missed-call-text-back-feature ; [K14b] Call Details trigger: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001212511-workflow-trigger-call-details

skills.name: crm-connect-playbook
skills.description: Use when connecting a CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, GoHighLevel, Zoho, Pipedrive, Close, Attio, monday, JobNimbus, or any CRM with docs and an API) and working inside it safely.
skills.content:
---
name: crm-connect-playbook
description: >-
  Use when connecting a CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, GoHighLevel, Zoho, Pipedrive,
  Close, Attio, monday, JobNimbus, or any CRM with docs and an API) and working
  inside it safely.
---
# Connect and work in any CRM

## Research
- Read the CRM's current official docs live: API, auth, rate limits, key objects, and whether there's an official connector or MCP server. Never rely on memory for a vendor's current API; these change fast.
- Write a short CRM map: objects, key fields, how auth works, what the user's plan allows. Cite doc links.
- If the plan has no API or connector, say so plainly and offer a fallback: CSV export or import, a spreadsheet mirror, or the plan's upgrade path.

## Connect
- Pick the simplest supported way in, in this order: (1) an official connector or plugin, (2) the vendor's official MCP server via OAuth, (3) an integration platform like Composio, (4) a personal API token as a last resort.
- Give one numbered step at a time, using real menu names from the docs. Don't invent menu paths.
- Ask for read-only scopes first. Add write scopes only when the user wants writes.
- Request any token through the app's masked secret request so it's saved as a bot secret. Never ask for a key in chat, never repeat it, and never write it into memory, a skill, or a file.
- Admin-only steps (enabling an MCP server, creating a private app) may need the CRM admin: give the user a short checklist to forward.

## Verify
- Run one read-only test, such as listing 5 recent contacts or deals, and show the result. It's only connected once that test passes.

## Work
- Read before write. For every create, edit, or update, show the exact change (record, field, old value to new value) and wait for a yes. Bulk changes get a count and a sample first.
- Never delete records, touch billing or user seats, or send customer emails or SMS. Customer messages are drafts the user approves and sends.
- Warn before heavy reads; rate limits and API credits vary by plan.
- Create routines (like a weekly pipeline summary or stale-deal check) only when asked, and stay quiet when there's nothing to report.
